entities.name: William d'Aubigny, 3rd Earl of Arundel
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
William d'Aubigny, 3rd Earl of Arundel (c. 1175–1221), also styled William de Albini IV, was an English magnate, favourite of King John, and crusader who took the cross for the Fifth Crusade. Holding the great honour of Arundel, he navigated the turbulent politics of John’s reign and Magna Carta’s aftermath.

Royal favour brought offices and marriages that tied the Aubigny line into the highest baronage. His eastern expedition linked English aristocratic piety to the failed Damietta campaign.

Arundel’s career maps baronial power between Angevin kingship and crusade.
